rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 7-8, Table F.3 and Figs 12-19 - the authors train and test their own fine-tuned VGG16 model on a 4263-image tomato pest dataset (8 pest classes, 80/10/10 split) and report 96.5% test accuracy against SGD/RMSProp/Adam/custom VGG16 comparators.
rows.notes: The paper is primarily a survey of DL and IoT for precision agriculture with one original experiment appended. That experiment is image-based classification of eight tomato pest species from a Mendeley camera-image dataset using transfer learning; it is not remote sensing, not weed detection, and it measures nothing about herbicide application or environmental effect. The statements about weed detection enabling precise spraying and reducing herbicides (Section 2.3) are narrative review of other work (Yu et al. 2019, Bah et al. 2018, Huang et al. 2020) and are not the authors' own results. At most the study's own result is an upstream detection capability (pest classification accuracy) for a different target (pests, not weeds) and a different sensing technology (hand/camera images, not remote sensing).

notes: Full text appears complete (survey sections 1-6, proposed model Section 7, results Section 8, conclusion, references). Classified as primary only because of the appended pest-classification experiment; the bulk of the document is a review and none of its own data bears on remote sensing for weed detection or herbicide reduction.
